paper_metadata.title: Entity linking for biomedical literature
paper_metadata.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making, 15(Suppl 1):S4
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper proposes an unsupervised collective-inference entity-linking approach for mapping mentions in full biomedical papers to entities from 300 ontologies. It uses ontology semantics and structure for similarity and ranking, reports a 9-percentage-point absolute linking-accuracy gain over a state-of-the-art supervised entity linker without manual annotation, and introduces a small biomedical benchmark.

problem_addressed: Biomedical entity linking: identify prominent entity mentions in unstructured full-text biomedical literature and ground them in knowledge-base or ontology reference entities. The work addresses scarce labeled biomedical EL data and insufficient context for ambiguous mentions, with the intended downstream benefit of enriching literature and supporting biological-process modelling.

methodology.description: Execution pipeline: (1) aggregate 300 BioPortal biology ontologies into a knowledge-base graph whose vertices are classes, individuals, and properties and whose edges are ontology triples; (2) extract prominent mentions using a name tagger, regex-based mention joining, and shallow noun-phrase parsing; (3) retrieve candidates through a surface-form dictionary made from labels, names, synonyms, aliases, and symbols; (4) pre-rank candidates using EntropyRank, a recursive, PageRank-like salience score weighted by entropy of ontology relation properties, with partial surface matches penalized using Jaccard similarity; (5) build a document graph linking mentions by sentence- or paragraph-level co-occurrence; (6) collectively score each mention–candidate pair using candidate salience plus matches between the candidate's ontology neighbors and the mention's document-graph neighbors; and (7) select the highest-scoring candidate. Experiments set α=15 and β=8.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The method is explicitly ontology-guided. It merges 300 BioPortal biology ontologies into a web of data with over 2 million entities and over 50 million factual statements. Ontology classes, properties, and individuals are candidate reference entities; ontology triples form the knowledge graph; labels, synonyms, aliases, and symbols populate the surface-form dictionary; relation-property entropy supplies edge weights; and ontology neighbor relations provide collective-disambiguation evidence.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured full-text biomedical literature, plus an aggregated biomedical ontology knowledge base.
input_output.input_granularity: Full documents; mentions are extracted as named entities and noun-phrase chunks, while collective context is evaluated at mention, sentence, or paragraph level.
input_output.output_representation: Entity mention-to-reference-entity links (grounded ontology/knowledge-base entities); the underlying KB representation is a graph of ontology triples.

metrics: Linking accuracy: for each correctly extracted mention, whether it is linked to the correct KB entry
baselines: Chan and Roth (2013) relational-inference wikifier, described as a state-of-the-art EL system trained on news-related data
Ablation/comparison by inference context: mention-level non-collective, sentence-level collective, and paragraph-level collective
evaluation.setting: A pilot benchmark on one extensively cited signal-transduction pathway paper (Lipniacki). Domain experts annotated links for 318 mentions/97 unique entities from 77 sentences. The authors evaluate linking accuracy only on correctly extracted mentions; both their system and UIUC Wikifier's associated mention extractor obtained 63% precision, 65% recall, and 64% F-measure. Context granularity was compared at mention, sentence, and paragraph level; the external supervised news-trained baseline was evaluated against the proposed sentence-level result.

value: Mention-level non-collective linking accuracy: 73.08%.
Sentence-level collective linking accuracy: 83.17%, a 10.09-point gain over mention-level inference.
Paragraph-level collective linking accuracy: 65.87%, 17.30 points below sentence-level inference; the authors attribute the decline to unrelated context/noise.

Against the news-trained Chan and Roth (2013) wikifier, the proposed system achieved 83.17% linking accuracy (173/208 correct links) versus 74.34% (84/113), an 8.83-point absolute gain, reported in the abstract as 9%.
The associated mention extraction component achieved 63% precision, 65% recall, and 64% F-measure.
